title: His Aunt Edna Sanders, who taught him time
summary: Green names his aunt as the one who taught him to keep time, and tells of her later WAC service, master's degree and death after a blow at the post office.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My Aunt Edna B. Sanders. She was the one was studying to be a teacher then in the men's school in Atlanta University. You see? She eventually became a WAC,

though, some years later, and a teacher. She got the Master's degrees and all these things, and that was here in New York City, from up over Sugar Hill, you know. She went to -- she went into the WACs and so forth. She was in there for a few years.

After she come out as a WAC, she finished and got her Master's degree and then -- then soon after then she passed, got accidentally harmed. She was working for the post office, and she got -- accidentally got struck in the temple by some -- some big -- one of the loaders, I guess you could call an elbow, you know, on the temple, and she never actually recovered from that blow, went into complications of some sort.
But anyhow I used to go out and make this money. I used to attract people's attention by dropping coins -- oops.
